'''Boyd''': {{legend0|#a5b0ff|40–50%}} {{legend0|#7996e2|50–60%}} {{legend0|#6674de|60–70%}} | title = Governor | before_election = [[Frank Keating]] | before_party = Republican Party (United States) | after_election = [[Frank Keating]] | after_party = Republican Party (United States) }} {{ElectionsOK}} The '''1998 Oklahoma gubernatorial election''' was held on November 3, 1998, and was a race for [[Governor of Oklahoma]]. Incumbent [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] [[Frank Keating]] won re-election in a landslide against [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic]] [[Oklahoma House of Representatives|State Representative]] [[Laura Boyd]]. The [[Reform Party (United States)|Reform Party]], the first alternative party to be able to run a candidate for governor in the state since [[1970 Oklahoma gubernatorial election|1970]], had Hoppy Heidelberg as its candidate.{{cite web| url = http://www.tulsaworld.com/news/ex-oc-bombing-juror-hoppy-heidelberg-to-run-for-governor/article_3a5beb8f-ca35-5b91-8f8a-1b5f8c9f2fc9.html| title = Ex-OC Bombing Juror Hoppy Heidelberg to Run for Governor {{!}} Latest Headlines {{!}} tulsaworld.com}} Heidelberg was removed from a gubernatorial debate that he disrupted after not being allowed to be a participant.{{cite news |last1=Hinton |first1=Mick |title=Reform Candidate Says He's Banned From OU |url=https://www.oklahoman.com/story/news/1998/10/27/reform-candidate-says-hes-banned-from-ou/62264470007/ |work=The Oklahoman |url-access=limited |date=October 27, 1998}} This was the first occasion since Oklahoma statehood that [[Bryan County, Oklahoma|Bryan]], [[Carter County, Oklahoma|Carter]], [[Cotton County, Oklahoma|Cotton]], [[Garvin County, Oklahoma|Garvin]], [[Greer County, Oklahoma|Greer]], [[Harmon County, Oklahoma|Harmon]], [[Jefferson County, Oklahoma|Jefferson]], [[Kiowa County, Oklahoma|Kiowa]], [[Love County, Oklahoma|Love]], [[Murray County, Oklahoma|Murray]], and [[Pontotoc County, Oklahoma|Pontotoc]] counties voted for a Republican for Governor, although several of these counties backed Independent candidate [[Wes Watkins]] four years earlier. This election marked the first time a woman received the nomination for governor from a major party in Oklahoma. It was also the first time a Republican was elected to a consecutive term ([[Henry Bellmon]] was the first Republican to serve two terms, though not consecutive). ==Primary election== Primary elections were held on August 25, 1998 with runoffs occurring on September 15, 1998, although no runoffs were required in the gubernatorial race. ===Republican party=== Incumbent governor [[Frank Keating]] was renominated without opposition after potential challenger Joe Vickers was removed from the primary ballot. Keating alleged that Vickers had changed his party registration from Democratic to Republican too late to appear on the Republican ballot. The state election board upheld Keating's challenge.{{cite news |last1=Hinton |first1=Mick |last2=English |first2=Paul |title=Keating Gets GOP Challenger Vickers Ousted From Race |url=https://www.oklahoman.com/story/news/1998/07/15/keating-gets-gop-challenger-vickers-ousted-from-race/62275616007/ |work=The Oklahoman |date=July 15, 1998 |url-access=limited}} ===Democratic party=== State representative [[Laura Boyd]] won the Democratic nomination over fellow representative [[James Hager]]. This was the first time since runoffs were reinstated in [[1946 Oklahoma gubernatorial election|1946]] that the Democratic primary for governor without an incumbent did not require a subsequent runoff.{{efn|No runoff was required in [[1982 Oklahoma gubernatorial election|1982]] when incumbent [[George Nigh]] faced only token opposition in the primary.}} ====Candidates==== *[[Laura Boyd]], member of [[Oklahoma House of Representatives]] from [[Norman, Oklahoma]] *[[James Hager]], member of [[Oklahoma House of Representatives]] from [[Pawhuska, Oklahoma]] ====Results==== {{Election box begin no change | title = Democratic primary results{{cite web |title=Oklahoma State Election Board, Primary Election Results, August 25, 1998 |url=https://oklahoma.gov/content/dam/ok/en/elections/election-results/1998-election-results/1998-primary-summary-results.pdf}}{{cite book |editor1-last=Ward |editor1-first=Lance |title=State of Oklahoma Election Results and Statistics 1998 |date=1998 |publisher=Oklahoma State Election Board |location=Oklahoma City |url=https://digitalprairie.ok.gov/digital/collection/stgovpub/id/13879 |access-date=8 January 2026}} }} {{Election box winning candidate with party link no change | candidate = [[Laura Boyd]] | party = Democratic Party (United States) | votes = 171,121 | percentage = 60.24% }} {{Election box candidate with party link no change | candidate = [[James Hager]] | party = Democratic Party (United States) | votes = 112,941 | percentage = 39.76% }} {{Election box total no change | votes = 284,062 | percentage= 100.00% }} {{Election box end}} ==General election== In addition to Keating and Boyd, Hoppy Heidelberg, a former member of the [[Oklahoma City Bombing]] [[grand jury]], ran on the [[Reform Party of the United States of America|Reform Party]] ticket. ===Results=== {{Election box begin | title=1998 gubernatorial election, Oklahoma{{cite web |title=State of Oklahoma Official Returns, General Election -
